=== FILE: gray_counter_equiv.eqy ===
# Equivalence setup: approved gray_counter.v (gold) vs approved
# gray_counter_refactor.v (gate). Both define module gray_counter with the
# same ports and the same state register name, so eqy matches by name.

[gold]
read_verilog gray_counter.v
prep -top gray_counter

[gate]
read_verilog gray_counter_refactor.v
prep -top gray_counter

[strategy simple]
use sat
depth 10

[strategy formal]
use sby
depth 10
engine smtbmc
=== END FILE ===

result.detail: The setup file sits at the top level, because the approved RTL is placed beside it and reading the RTL from a subfolder (../) would be refused as outside the setup's folder. I wrote no files named gray_counter.v or gray_counter_refactor.v. Equivalence compares only the two versions against each other: a bug present in both versions would not be detected, and the Gray-code behaviour itself is not checked against a specification here. After a pass, a good follow-up is to run this setup against a mutant gate, for example a wrong wrap code or a wrong flip bit, to confirm that the setup actually examines both outputs. The cited knowledge document's independent check is still marked pending.
